newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures steady, turn attention to U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures steady, turn attention to U.S. CPI.

text.p: German Bunds were steady in late trade, turning their attention from what turned out to be uneventful U.S. producer price data to consumer price figures due on Thursday.

Bunds, which have underperformed Treasuries of late, closely tracked their U.S. counterparts after core PPI fell 0.3 percent in October. The December DTB contract traded down three basis points in late trade at 100.69.
But traders remain bullish on German debt, expecting the the contract to move toward 101.00 as long as Treasuries do not pull world debt markets down.

Traders said there is little risk of profit-taking after what has been a strong rise in recent weeks. Rather, they said, investors are looking for opportunities to buy the market on dips, limiting any downside.
The Bund spread, however, eased to its lowest level since mid-August relative to Treasuries on the day as the spread hit 41 basis points, down from 46 basis points.

A pair of Bundesbankers Franz-Christoph Zeitler and Olaf Sievert both threw water on any immediate need to cut interest rates, but the yield curve was little changed. The spread between five and 10-year debt was steady at 126 basis points.
Bund traders are keeping a close eye on foreign exchange markets.

Further mark strength could lead the Bundesbank to cut interest rates, or at least talk up the chances of a rate cut, to undermine the German currency and provide relief to German export companies, they said.
